## About

Collages (25 × 2 inches) and tall strips in galleries, as subfigures, and
in a layout div. The same shapes on their own, and the `fit` option, are
on [`h-wide`](h-wide.html).

Wide figures open at screen height from the left end, tall ones at screen
width from the top. In a gallery, left and right arrow pan a wide figure
(and do nothing on a tall strip) instead of changing the image; the
previous and next buttons change it.

The cases below draw with these helpers:

```{r}
# A collage: `n` panels side by side, like a wide patchwork figure.
collage <- function(n = 12) {
  set.seed(1)
  par(mfrow = c(1, n), mar = c(3, 3, 2, 1))
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    plot(cumsum(rnorm(200)), type = "l", main = paste("Panel", i),
         xlab = "", ylab = "", col = hcl.colors(n)[i], lwd = 2)
  }
}

# A tall strip: `n` rows stacked, like a tall patchwork figure.
# Each seed gets its own palette (without its lightest end), so different
# strips look different.
strip <- function(seed = 2, n = 8) {
  set.seed(seed)
  palette <- c("Viridis", "Plasma", "Zissou 1", "Dark 3", "Sunset", "Cividis", "Dynamic", "Inferno")[(seed - 2) %% 8 + 1]
  par(mfrow = c(n, 1), mar = c(2, 3, 2, 1))
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    plot(cumsum(rnorm(100)), type = "l", main = paste0("Strip ", seed, ", row ", i),
         xlab = "", ylab = "", col = hcl.colors(n + 2, palette)[i], lwd = 2)
  }
}
```

## 1. Gallery of two collages {#c1 expect-fit="height"}

Left/Right and drags pan along the collage; the previous and next
buttons switch collages.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: collages
#| fig-width: 25
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "First collage."
#|   - "Second collage."

collage(n = 12)
collage(n = 15)
```

## 2. Gallery of two tall strips {#c2 expect-fit="width"}

Each strip opens at screen width and extends downwards. The left and right
arrow keys do nothing (there is nowhere to go sideways) instead of
changing strips; the previous and next buttons change them.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: strips
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "First strip."
#|   - "Second strip."

strip(seed = 8, n = 8)
strip(seed = 9, n = 8)
```

## 3. Stacked collages {#c3 expect-fit="height"}

Each subfigure in this layout opens on its own at screen height, and the
two form a gallery.

```{r}
#| label: fig-collage-rows
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 25
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-cap: "Two collages, stacked."
#| fig-subcap: ["First collage", "Second collage"]
#| layout-nrow: 2

collage(n = 12)
collage(n = 15)
```

## 4. Strips side by side {#c4 expect-fit="width"}

```{r}
#| label: fig-strip-cols
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15
#| fig-cap: "Two tall strips, side by side."
#| fig-subcap: ["First strip", "Second strip"]
#| layout-ncol: 2

strip(seed = 2, n = 8)
strip(seed = 3, n = 8)
```

## 5. Tall strips in a layout div {#c5 expect-fit="width"}

A `.panzoom` div with a layout wraps two separate code cells. Each strip
opens on its own, with no gallery, since they are not subfigures.

::: {.panzoom layout-ncol="2"}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15

strip(seed = 4, n = 8)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15

strip(seed = 5, n = 8)
```

:::


## 6. Collages of different lengths {#c6 expect-fit="height"}

Two cells, a long collage (40 × 2 in, 24 panels) and a shorter one
(24 × 2 in, 12 panels), joined by `group`. Each opens at screen height
from its left end; stepping to the other image fits it afresh, so the
short collage doesn't keep the long one's scale or position. Whether a
figure counts as a strip depends only on its shape (much shorter, and
the short one would open whole on the test's 2560 px wide screen), so
`fig-dpi: 48` halves the resolution to keep the files small. The
captions differ in length, so stepping between the two changes the caption
band's height, and each collage must stay clear of it.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: mixed-collages
#| fig-width: 40
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-dpi: 48
#| fig-cap: "The long collage."

collage(n = 24)
```

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: mixed-collages
#|   description: "A longer text under the short collage, so that the caption band grows when the gallery steps to it. Each panel is a random walk of 200 steps, colored along a single palette from the first panel to the last, and titled with its panel number so the order can be read at any zoom."
#| fig-width: 24
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-dpi: 48
#| fig-cap: "The short collage, with a description."

collage(n = 12)
```

## 7. Strips of different lengths {#c7 expect-fit="width"}

This is case 4 with strips of different sizes, 4 × 20 in (10 rows) and 3 ×
12 in (6 rows), in a layout div, with captions of different lengths. Each
opens at screen width from its top, and the layout shows them at different
heights on the page.

::: {.panzoom layout-ncol="2"}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 20
#| fig-cap: "The long strip."

strip(seed = 6, n = 10)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 3
#| fig-height: 12
#| fig-cap: "The short strip, with a caption long enough to wrap onto a second line in the viewer."

strip(seed = 7, n = 6)
```

:::
